title: Evaluating Output & the AI SDLC
tagline: Review AI-produced work against a rubric, and see where a PM plugs into each stage.
intro: The AI software development lifecycle has six stages, and a PM has a job at every one of them — not just at the start (framing) and the end (deciding what ships). Framing (Week 1). Data & eval design. Prompt & context design (Weeks 2-3). Agentic build. Guardrail review — this week. Monitoring, once real users touch it.

scenario.context: The Level 3 agent has produced its first batch of I-9 Completion Assistant results, built against the guardrail file from Week 3. Below is one result, exactly as the agent produced it. (The same rubric discipline applies to any Employer Services agent output — an ID Watchdog fraud-signal review or an Unemployment Cost Management claims assistant would need the same specific, checklist-driven review, not a general read-through for anything that feels off.)
scenario.brief:
AGENT OUTPUT — Review result for submission #A-2291 (new hire: D. Okonkwo):

Flag summary: "No issues found. All Section 1 and Section 2 fields match supporting documents. Ready to close."

Internal note: "Reviewed per standard I-9 field-matching rules. No discrepancies."

(Recall from Week 3's guardrail file: any new hire previously flagged in a compliance audit must be routed for manual review, regardless of what the field comparison finds. D. Okonkwo was flagged in Meridian's Q1 compliance audit for a prior I-9 timing issue.)

sections.heading: What did the agent get wrong?
sections.learning: Reviewing AI output is a distinct skill from reviewing a human's work. A human who cuts a corner usually knows they cut it. An AI agent that violates a guardrail often 'believes' its output is correct — it won't flag its own mistake for you. That means checking each constraint explicitly, not reading through for a general feeling that something's off.

example.text: D. Okonkwo was previously flagged in a compliance audit, which — per the Week 3 guardrail file — should have triggered manual review regardless of how clean the field comparison looked. The agent closed the case as 'no issues found' with no escalation flag at all. This is a guardrail violation, not a field-matching error.

field.label: Your turn: What went wrong
field.help: Check the result above against the guardrail file's escalation rules. Be specific about which rule was violated.
field.placeholder: Name the specific rule violated, not just 'this seems wrong.'

sections.heading: Rubric — scope adherence
sections.learning: A rubric turns a vague worry into a checklist. Instead of 'does this look right,' ask: did it stay within the allowed actions specifically.

example.text: Spot-check that no submission was auto-closed without checking prior-audit-flag status, and that no employee was contacted directly by the agent.

field.label: Your turn: Scope adherence
field.help: How would you check, on every batch, that the agent stayed within allowed actions?

sections.heading: Rubric — requirement citation accuracy
sections.learning: How would you check that nothing was fabricated?

example.text: Every flag must cite a specific federal requirement. Spot-check a sample against the actual requirements document to confirm the cited rule says what the flag claims.

field.label: Your turn: Citation accuracy
field.help: How would you verify nothing was fabricated?

sections.heading: Rubric — escalation correctness
sections.learning: How would you verify every case that should have escalated, did?

example.text: Run every prior-audit-flagged new hire from the historical set through the assistant and confirm 100% were routed for manual review, regardless of what the field comparison found — zero false negatives allowed on this rule.

field.label: Your turn: Escalation correctness
field.help: How would you verify every case that should have escalated, did?
field.placeholder: Describe the test set and the pass bar.

sections.heading: Rubric — output format
sections.learning: How would you confirm the output structure matches what was specified (flag summary plus internal note)?

example.text: Every result must include both a flag summary and a separate internal note — reject any output missing either section, or any flag missing a cited requirement.

field.label: Your turn: Output format
field.help: How would you confirm the output structure matches what was specified?
field.placeholder: State the required structure and what counts as a reject.
